issues.desc: Ghidra decompiled this as __cdecl void with bare 'return;' everywhere, dropping the EAX return values (systematic EAX-tracking bug). The disassembly shows real int returns: most paths XOR EAX,EAX;RET (return 0), but the field-command path @0x118C1-0x118D9 does 'do{r=fd2_field_command_menu_loop();}while(r==0); if(r==1) r^=1; return r;' (MOV EAX,EBX;RET). The single caller fd2_main @0x25DCE consumes EAX (MOV ESI,EAX then TEST ESI;JZ re-invoke), so the return value is load-bearing: a 0 return makes fd2_main loop back into fd2_game_main_loop, non-zero exits. Emitted as int accordingly. Also: the two dispatch-table calls (per_chapter_post_action_handler @0x51B19 and ai_post_action_consequence @0x51B91) push ESI (=selected char idx uVar2) before CALL (PUSH ESI;CALL;ADD ESP,4), so they are invoked with (uVar2); Ghidra rendered them as '()' with no arg ��� emitted with (sel) per disasm + the (uint32) table prototype in globals.h. Recommend post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical return-value computation and the table-call argument.

AP/DP x1.15 buff. Assembly @0x1B7EF-0x1B819 = FILD/FMUL m64[0x5018D]/CALL __CHP/FISTP. __CHP (0x377A4) sets FPU RC=11 (round-toward-zero) then FRNDINT, so the value is TRUNCATED before FISTP stores it ��� i.e. assembly truncates, it does NOT round-to-nearest. The emitted C (int)((double)x * 1.15) ALSO truncates toward zero, so the rounding DIRECTION matches. Residual concern is only Watcom 9.5a codegen precision (x87 80-bit FMUL vs C 64-bit double intermediate); for unit-test ground-truth this is bypassed by choosing bases where 80-bit and 64-bit truncation agree (100->114, 200->229, tested in testbtl.c). Still recommend a post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL/__CHP/FISTP emission. [reviewer KEEP-confirmed valid] Precision-ordering refinement: the FMUL at 0x1B7F3 runs BEFORE __CHP sets PC=64-bit, so it uses the entry control-word precision. Cross-check: bases 100->114 and 200->229 agree at 64-bit and exact-80-bit truncation; base 40 would give 46 at 64-bit but 45 at exact-80-bit and was correctly AVOIDED in the tests. Unit tests pass under real Watcom, empirically confirming truncation; a post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL/__CHP/FISTP emission remains the recommended final check. No code change needed.

Unit test for the high-risk numeric/branch paths of fd2_dpmi_alloc_dos_memory (CF success/failure branch; the three output computations out_segment=eax<<16 / out_linear=(eax&0xFFFF)<<4 / out_selector=edx&0xFFFF; the off-by-one page-lock arithmetic lock(seg>>12, paragraphs*16+(seg>>12)-1)) is DEFERRED to Phase 9 integration. Reason (proven, not convenience): these paths are reachable only via int386(), which has no deterministic unit-test seam in the DOS/4GW harness. (1) A test-local int386 override to inject the DPMI host result was implemented and proven by bisection to deterministically crash/hang the DOS/4GW runtime -- overriding the CRT int386 breaks the extender's protected-mode interrupt reflection that the CRT itself depends on, so the test executable faults before reaching the dpmi suite; with the override disabled the same build completes (369 pass + the 3 dpmi tests fail on real DPMI non-determinism). int386 is also used by src/input/input.c, whose suite depends on the real INT 16h. issues.desc: Ghidra EAX-tracking artifact resolved by reading asm. After fread(backbuf,1,0xAD,fp) (CALL 0x37072 -> EAX=bytes read) the asm does MOV AX,word ptr [ESI+0xa5] (0x204ea) overwriting only the low 16 bits of EAX, then MOV [ESP+0x10],EAX (0x204f1). The decomp renders this as frame_count_pack = CONCAT22((short)(uVar3>>0x10), *(undefined2*)(backbuf+0xa5)) and the loop uses (short)frame_count_pack -- i.e. only the low 16 bits, sign-extended. The high 16 bits (the fread return leftover) are dead. Emitted cleanly as int16 frame_count = *(int16*)(backbuf+0xA5); loop `for(i=0;i<(int)frame_count;i++)`. Semantically exact; verified against real ANI.DAT (anim 0 header[0xA5]=96, anim 1=51).

issues.desc: AoE scatter X/Y. Assembly @0x21E1A-0x21E38 (X) and 0x21E64-0x21E80 (Y) do FLD cos/sin + FILD radius + FMUL + FILD origin + FADDP (+FADD m64[0x50200] for Y) + CALL __CHP + FISTP. __CHP @0x377A4 sets RC=11 (round-toward-zero) via OR-high-byte-0x1F then FRNDINT, so the value is TRUNCATED toward zero before FISTP. Emitted C uses plain (int)(double) casts which also truncate toward zero, so the rounding DIRECTION matches. Residual concern is only Watcom 9.5a codegen precision: the x87 FMUL/FADD run at the entry control-word precision (80-bit internal) whereas the emitted C uses 64-bit double intermediates, so a result whose true value sits within ~1 ULP of an integer could truncate to a different integer. The two unit tests bypass this by choosing RNG seeds (0x1234 radius1 ang133, 0x5555 radius6 ang293) whose X/Y fractional parts are ~0.32-0.73 of a pixel from any integer boundary, where 64-bit and 80-bit truncation agree; the RNG seed sequence itself was confirmed exact via Ghidra emulate_function on 0x4E893. The deg->rad factor is the binary literal 0.0174532 (af99d76c40df913f @0x501F8), emitted verbatim. Recommend a post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL/FADDP/__CHP/FISTP emission and the 0.0174532 / -8.0 constant fixups.

The normal path has no explicit RET: the function tail-JMPs (JMP 0x18888 @0x2246b) into the MIDDLE of an adjacent function, fd2_render_decimal_number_to_buffer @0x187d6. 0x18888 is that function's standard Watcom epilogue tail (ADD ESP,0x1C / POP EBP / POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX / RET), which is byte-identical to the epilogue this function's own prologue (PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP + SUB ESP,0x1C) would require, so the Watcom 9.5a compiler shared it (the same 0x18888 tail is also reached from fd2_blit_scaled_tile_map_view @0x1f6a5). Emitted as a plain 'return;'; the compiler regenerates the matching epilogue. issues.desc: The 10-entry table data_fd2_battle_spell_cast_cinematic_phase_handler_table @ 0x523B9 is called via FF /4 indirect jump (CALL dword ptr [EAX*4+0x523b9], EAX=spell_id) with 5 args pushed + ADD ESP,0x14, result used in EAX as a frame count. Ghidra masks the args (renders each call as "()") because it lacks the fn-ptr signature. Reconstructed from the disassembly + decompiling handler[0] (fd2_tick_summon_spell_setup_pre_animation_8slot @ 0x26152: param_count=5, returns int): signature int(uint32 caster_idx, uint32 caster_sprite, uint32 work_buf, uint32 stride, uint32 phase_code). globals.h table type changed void(*)(void) -> int(*)(uint32,uint32,uint32,uint32,uint32). All 10 sites reconstructed: phase_code = per-site immediate (pre-cast bound 0, pre-cast loop body 1 then 2; per-target bound 3, inner always 4, inner miss 5, inner hit 5; post-cast bound 6, post loop body 7 then 8); arg1=caster_idx, arg2=team_caster_sprite (FDOTHER team sprite, decompiler puVar5), arg3=work-buffer ptr matching the adjacent blit (work / work+0x4ba0 / swap_buf), arg4=stride 0x140 (full-frame) or 0x280 (wide composite).

The 6 function-local const tables (shake_x_offsets[4], shake_y_row_offsets[4], hp_lerp_hits[10], player_team_sprite_id[9], enemy_team_sprite_id[10], intro_sfx_bank[10]) are indexed by spell_id. The inline path runs for spell_id in 0x00..0x17,0x19..0x1B, so spell_id can exceed a table length (e.g. earth attack spells 0x0A/0x0B/0x0C reach the hit branch that reads hp_lerp_hits[spell_id], which has only 10 entries). In the original this is a latent OOB read of adjacent stack locals (the disassembly REP MOVSD-copies each table from .rodata onto the stack at distinct, non-contiguous offsets, so the over-read picks up neighboring stack/gap bytes). It only feeds the cosmetic HP-bar lerp divisor and the sprite/SFX index selection -- the applied damage (written by fd2_calc_magic_damage) is unaffected. Emitted as non-static initialized const local arrays indexed by spell_id, preserving the source-level OOB. The exact over-read byte is Watcom-stack-layout dependent in BOTH original and rebuild (Layer-2 target, not byte-exact); spells 0x00..0x09 are fully in-bounds and deterministic.

HP-bar lerp uses signed 32-bit IDIV: hp_current = starting_hp - (int16)((int)(starting_hp - final_hp) * hit_count / hp_lerp_hits[spell_id]). Both HP snapshots are sign-extended from int16 (MOVSX word [tgt+0x40]); multiply+divide are 32-bit signed (CDQ/IDIV @0x2aef2/0x2aef5); the quotient is subtracted from starting_hp and stored back truncated to int16. Emitted with explicit (int)/(int16) casts to force the same signed widths. Flag for compile+disasm confirmation that Watcom 9.5a emits IDIV (not unsigned DIV).

The summon (spell_id>=0x20) and special-attack (0x18 / 0x1C..0x1F) branches CALL the worker then JMP into the shared function epilogue (0x2b5d6: ADD ESP,0x130 / POP EBP/EDI/ESI/EBX / RET) rather than a separate RET. Emitted as plain early return after each call. The inline path falls through to the same epilogue, emitted as the natural end-of-function return. Equivalence relies on Watcom 9.5a regenerating an equivalent frame teardown; functionally identical (cdecl, caller cleans args, void return).

FIXED (reviewer-blocking, corrected in src/anim/anispell.c). shake_y_dir (decompiler palette_y_dir_sign, stack [ESP+0x104]) is computed from the freshly-advanced RNG seed left in EAX by fd2_advance_rng_state @0x4e893, NOT from flash_unit. Disasm 0x2af40-0x2af58: CALL 0x0004e893 ; MOV EDX,EAX ; MOV EBX,0x3 ; SAR EDX,0x1f ; IDIV EBX ; MOV EAX,0x1 ; SUB EAX,EDX ; MOV [ESP+0x104],EAX -- the value divided by 3 is the CALL's EAX return. fd2_advance_rng_state (XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AX,[0x627B8] / ADD AX,0x9014 / ROL AX,1 x3 / MOV [0x627B8],AX / RET) returns the new seed zero-extended in EAX, range [0,0xFFFF]. Ghidra mis-attributed the IDIV operand to uVar6/flash_unit because fd2_advance_rng_state was decompiled as void (documented EAX-after-CALL tracking bug). protos.h already prototypes it as uint32 fd2_advance_rng_state(void) and battle.c notes 'callers use return value'; many sibling sites (battle.c, anisummn.c) already consume the return. Emitter originally copied the decompiler bug as 'shake_y_dir = 1 - (int)flash_unit % 3;' which discarded the RNG result and used a different value. Corrected to 'shake_y_dir = 1 - (int)fd2_advance_rng_state() % 3;' which matches the disassembly (IDIV operand = the CALL's EAX) byte-for-byte in semantics and matches the established codebase convention (consume EAX return directly rather than re-read [0x627B8]). The reviewer's alternative fix (call then re-read data_fd2_shared_rng_seed) yields an identical value (EAX == stored seed, both [0,0xFFFF], both promote to the same non-negative int) but introduces a memory re-read not present in the original; the EAX-return form is the faithful one. shake_y_dir feeds only the cosmetic per-target shake X-offset sign (shake_x_offsets[shake_idx] * shake_y_dir); applied damage is unaffected.

Handler indexes a 5-byte local item-id table by the cursor tile terrain-class byte (item_id_table[tile_attr], 0xb5 sprite offset). The terrain class is the low byte of fd2_read_tile_attribute_at_pos out_buf[+2] (terrain_byte & 0x1F), range 0..0x1F, so classes 5..0x1F index past the 5-entry table. In the binary this is the literal frame read *(byte*)((int)&var_14 + var_1a) into the adjacent stack frame; the emitted C item_id_table[tile_attr] reads whatever the compiler lays out after item_id_table[5]. For real game data only classes 0..4 occur on a pickup tile (and the slot is unreferenced by any chapter FDFIELD hook, so it is never reached with live tile data), making classes 0..4 byte-identical; the out-of-range case is frame-layout dependent and would need a post-build disasm of this frame to confirm bit-identity. Low risk: dead/cut content path, in-range cases exact.

Behavioral unit test for fd2_main is DEFERRED to Phase 9 integration (reason proven, not convenience). fd2_main unconditionally issues int386(0x10,...) twice -- INT 10h video mode 0x13 on entry and mode 3 at shutdown -- through the REAL linked Watcom int386. issues.desc: Radial x/y coords use the cos/sin FPU idiom FILD/FMUL/FLD(cos|sin result)/FILD word/FMULP/FADD(P)/__CHP/FISTP at 0x26fa7-0x26ff6 (x) and 0x27005-0x27044 (y). __CHP @0x377A4 sets FPU RC=truncate-toward-zero before FISTP, so the binary TRUNCATES (does not round-to-nearest); emitted C uses (int)(double_expr), which also truncates toward zero, so the rounding DIRECTION matches (same proven pattern as 0x1b750 / 0x15b77). The angle is computed single-precision: binary does FILD dword(i*0x48) / FMUL float[0x3C8EFA2D] / FSTP double, i.e. a float*float product (in x87 80-bit) stored to a 64-bit double then passed to cos/sin; emitted as the identical-shape expression angle_rad = (double)((float)(i*0x48) * pi180.f) with pi180.f bit-cast from the exact 0x3C8EFA2D (value 0.017453277, NOT the textbook pi/180 0.0174532925). Residual concern is ONLY Watcom 9.5a codegen: (a) whether it keeps the float*float product in the 80-bit register before the (double) cast (matching FSTP double) rather than rounding to float first (double-rounding), and (b) x87 80-bit cos/sin/FMUL intermediates vs C 64-bit double. Unit tests bypass this by asserting the libm-INDEPENDENT acc==0 case (cos/sin terms multiplied by 0 -> x=sweep, y=30 exact) plus all integer-only state-4/5 blit-coord arithmetic; the cos/sin-derived non-zero coords are NOT hard-asserted offline. Tests run under the real Watcom 9.5a + its CLIB cos/sin (same routines as the game binary @0x3c885/0x3c898), all PASS. Recommend post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL float/FSTP double + __CHP/FISTP emission for the angle and both coord stores.

issues.desc: page_base = (fd2_check_party_has_char_id(0xC) ^ 1) * 3 is a genuine CALL-return consumption at the EAX-bug-risk site -- after CALL fd2_check_party_has_char_id; ADD ESP,4 the disassembly does XOR AL,1; MOV AH,3; MUL AH (8-bit, AX = AL*AH) and then MOVZX EBX,AL takes the low byte as page_base. The XOR AL,1 operates on the genuine byte return of the CALL (the callee returns MOV EAX,1 / XOR EAX,EAX, i.e. 0 or 1), so this is NOT a Ghidra EAX-tracking artifact; the emit deliberately encodes the value as the real return of fd2_check_party_has_char_id rather than trusting any decompiler extraout/stale-EAX rendering. The emit writes page_base = (int)((((fd2_check_party_has_char_id(0xc) & 0xff) ^ 1) * 3) & 0xff); the inner &0xff documents the byte-domain XOR AL,1, and the outer &0xff documents the MOVZX EBX,AL low-byte truncation of the 8-bit MUL result (both are semantic no-ops for the only reachable inputs 0/1 -> page_base in {0,3}, but keep the arithmetic in the same domain as the assembly). page_base+1 and page_base+2 mirror LEA EAX,[EBX+1] and ADD EBX,2. Needs a compile to confirm Watcom 9.5a regenerates the (retval^1)*3 byte computation and the +1/+2 page indices equivalently (vs e.g. promoting to a different width or reordering).

issues.desc: 0x3c964 is the DOS LE Entry Point (LE header EIP=0x3c964; Ghidra xref "From Entry Point [EXTERNAL]", 0 FD2 callers). Original body = single 2-byte short JMP (EB 78) over the 0x78-byte "WATCOM C/C++32..." copyright string at 0x3c966..0x3c9dd into the cstart body crt_equivalent_dos_main_bootstrap @ 0x3c9de (a SEPARATE emit target, same target file crt/crt.c). Ghidra's decompiler renders 0x3c964 as the entire 435-byte bootstrap (it falls through the JMP target boundary and inlines the separate function); that decompiled text is a DECOMPILER FRAGMENT of 0x3c9de, not of this thunk -- the disasm shows the true body is only `JMP 0x3c9de`. Emitted (mirroring crt_equivalent_get_eflags_thunk @ 0x37f86) as a REAL out-of-line function crt_equivalent_entry_start (owns a genuine PUBDEF for the LE Entry Point to reference) whose body invokes a #pragma aux in-line helper crt_entry_jmp_to_dos_main_bootstrap = "jmp crt_equivalent_dos_main_bootstrap". The transfer MUST be a JMP not a CALL: the bootstrap reads the loader's entry stack/registers (captures entry ESP at [0x52804]/[0x52818]; derives the DOS/4GW cmdline frame from &stack[+4]); a CALL would push a 4-byte return address and shift all of those entry-stack reads, so a C `return crt_equivalent_dos_main_bootstrap();` is NOT equivalent. crt_equivalent_entry_start is void(void) with no locals -> Watcom emits no __CHK stack-probe prologue, so ESP reaches the bootstrap exactly as the loader left it; the helper's JMP transfers control away permanently so the wrapper's own RET is never reached (matching the original, which has no RET). Three integration-time notes, none a behavioral risk: (1) Layer 3 only -- the rebuild's Watcom cstart will regenerate the JMP-over-copyright structure for the _cstart_ pair; the project does not pursue byte-exact, the Layer-2 contract (control reaches the bootstrap with ESP unperturbed) is met. (2) Watcom 9.5a emits no standalone symbol for a pragma-aux in-line helper, so the helper expands in place with no PUBDEF; the wrapper supplies the real PUBDEF crt_equivalent_entry_start that the LE header Entry Point binds to at wlink integration -- confirm crt.obj exports it and the LE header EIP resolves to it. (3) crt_equivalent_dos_main_bootstrap is done:false (not yet emitted); for the test build (genbuild links ALL of src/*.obj) the symbol is satisfied by a link-only counter stub in tests/testglob.c (the thunk is never executed at LE entry in tests; testmain.c is the test entry). The stub bumps g_cstart_bootstrap_entered so the crt/crt.c suite asserts the thunk's JMP actually reaches the bootstrap (test_entry_start_jumps_to_bootstrap) and returns stack-balanced as a tail call (test_entry_start_clean_tailcall_return, direct + via function pointer). When the real bootstrap @ 0x3c9de is emitted, remove the testglob stub + g_cstart_bootstrap_entered (the real bootstrap supersedes them) and re-point those two assertions or fold them into the bootstrap's own suite.

The fixed-point camera interpolation (intro 0x2014a-0x201a1 and outro 0x20309-0x20362) computes each axis as ((delta * ratio) round-toward-zero / 8) + base, where the binary materializes the round-toward-zero divide-by-8 with the SHL EDX,3 / SBB EAX,EDX / SAR EAX,3 idiom (sign in EDX, CF correction). Emitted as plain signed C 'delta * ratio / 8' which IS exactly round-toward-zero in C89, so it is behaviorally equivalent for ALL inputs; moreover every fixed-point input is pre-scaled by 0x600 (= 1536, a multiple of 8) and base = origin*0xC00 + max*0x600 is likewise a multiple of 8, so (delta*ratio) is always a multiple of 8 and the division is EXACT (the rounding correction is never actually exercised by valid game data). Watcom 9.5a may re-emit this as a bare SAR-by-3 (valid because the value is non-negative-or-exact) rather than the original SHL/SBB/SAR sequence; the difference is byte-level only and cannot diverge in result. verify_method: post-build -d disasm of the two zoom loops to confirm the camera args match the binary for the reachable (multiple-of-8) inputs; no behavioral risk.

Per-row scanline half-width = trunc(sqrt(r*r - dy*dy) * scale_num / 10.0). Assembly @0x21A54-0x21A83 = FILD r2_minus_dy2 / CALL sqrt(0x3C6FC) / FILD scale_num / FMULP / FDIV m64[0x501F0]=10.0 / CALL __CHP(0x377A4) / FISTP. __CHP loads CW high byte 0x1F (RC=11 round-toward-zero, PC=11 64-bit) then FRNDINT, so the value is TRUNCATED toward zero before FISTP stores it (the Ghidra ROUND() macro is misleading; this is NOT round-to-nearest). Emitted C (uint32)(int32)(sqrt((double)x)*scale_num/10.0) likewise truncates toward zero in C89, so the rounding DIRECTION matches exactly. Residual concern is only Watcom 9.5a x87 codegen precision: the original keeps sqrt/FMULP/FDIV intermediates in 80-bit registers while the C sqrt() return is a 64-bit double (the FMULP/FDIV themselves still run on the 80-bit x87 stack). For the unit-test ground-truth this is bypassed by choosing radii/dy where sqrt(r*r-dy*dy)*scale_num/10 is either an exact integer (sqrt(64)=8, sqrt(9)=3) or lies >0.2 away from any integer boundary (sqrt(39)=6.24, sqrt(48)=6.92, sqrt(55)=7.41), so 64-bit vs 80-bit truncation cannot diverge. Same mitigation pattern as the 0x1B750 / __CHP truncation entry.

The Ghidra decomp's last-3-args (param_3,sheet,sprite_idx) are the systematic EAX/param-shuffle artifact; the 3x 'PUSH [ESP+0x18]' @0x29381-0x29389 resolve (at each grown-stack point) to args 5/4/3 = palette_op/dst_stride/dst_buf, so the real call shape is as stated. Body is emit-ready and correct; all three workarounds (renamed/_impl/static stub; src test-hook; skip-link) are banned and were refused. CANNOT land as an isolated single-function commit because: (1) a LIVE testglob spy-mock defines fd2_blit_indexed_sprite (tests/testglob.c:1161-1181, recording _calls/_last_frame/_last_x/_last_y + _frame_log[128]); (2) link order blitspr.obj (test.lnk:31) precedes testglob.obj (:43), so emitting the real body keeps the spy as a Watcom W1027 redefinition WARNING -> 0-warning gate fails -> the spy MUST be deleted; (3) deleting the spy breaks 64 ASSERT_EQ (plus the slideshow frame_log loop, ~132 refs) across 4 ALREADY-APPROVED suites that use the mock purely as an arg-recorder for OTHER emitted callers' positional/frame logic: tests/gfx/rndscene.c (fd2_render_summon_aura_sprite_ring, 25 refs), tests/anim/aniend.c (slideshow 0x65-frame ordering + fanfare, 9 refs), tests/anim/anisumm1.c (54 refs), tests/anim/anisumm2.c (44 refs). Those callers pass sprite_handle=0 / dummy sheets, so the REAL body would deref a near-NULL offset table and fault, and it populates none of the g_blit_indexed_sprite_* spies. The sanctioned fix re-homes the 4 suites onto the g_rle_blit_* spy with real seeded sheets (valid +8 offset table so frame index is recoverable as g_rle_blit_last_sprite - sheet - 9; ushort headers). CRITICAL batch-ordering fact: the next-lower boundary fd2_rle_blit_sprite @0x4e63d is ALSO done:false (same phase-3 gfx/blitspr.c leaf-blit cluster of 20 pending fns incl. save/restore-block, sprite-with-stride). Re-homing onto g_rle_blit_* while rle_blit_sprite is itself the next domino just relocates the identical coupling one level deeper (123+ g_rle_blit assertions across rndstat/blitspr/battle2/rsrc). So this is a leaf-cluster batch-landing problem requiring orchestrator scheduling of the coordinated multi-file unit, NOT an isolated emitter turn. Coordinated unit (orchestrator to authorize): (a) emit real body into src/gfx/blitspr.c (base +8, uint16 dims, __CHK(0x20) prologue omitted); (b) delete the testglob.c spy-mock lines 1161-1181 + its scattered unused 'extern g_blit_indexed_sprite_*' decl blocks (22 decl-only files are harmless but should be cleaned); (c) add this dispatcher's own tests in tests/gfx/blitspr.c at the g_rle_blit_* boundary (offset-table base +8, uint16 width/height pass-through, palette_op pass-through, rle_stream=sprite_data+9), mirroring the existing test_indexed_xy_offset_and_arg_routing; (d) re-home the 4 dependent suites onto g_rle_blit_* with seeded sheets; (e) fix the misleading protos.h:212 prototype param names (atlas/frame_idx/x/y/mode -> sheet_ptr/sprite_idx/dst_buf/dst_stride/palette_op). Best landed together with the rle_blit_sprite leaf to avoid a double re-home.

issues.desc: The binary copies each of the three chapter-3 end scene placement tables (X/Y/facing, 7 bytes each @ 0x520BA/0x520C1/0x520C8) into an on-stack 7-byte block with an inlined MOVSD+MOVSW+MOVSB sequence (4+2+1 bytes) at 0x2310A-0x23125. Emitted as a plain byte-wise for(i<7) copy loop into uint8 recruit_block_a/b/c[7]. The copied bytes and their order are identical; the only difference is instruction selection (Watcom 9.5a may regenerate this as REP MOVS / unrolled MOVs / a byte loop). Result is provably byte-identical and the destination is only ever read back as a byte array by the callee fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro (target[i] for i in 0..6), so no aliasing/width risk. The unit test test_chapter_03_end_survivor_alive_recruits asserts the exact 21 bytes reach the callee. verify_method: post-build -d disasm of 0x230F2 to confirm the three 7-byte block contents match the binary; no behavioral risk.

The 4-byte LX-magic stack slot is pre-filled with the constant 0x00002020 before the 2-byte magic read overwrites its low 2 bytes. The binary materializes this as a memory load from a rodata constant adjacent to code: MOV EAX,[0x000360ff] (the dword at 0x360ff is 20 20 00 00) / MOV [slot],EAX @0x3634d-0x36352. Emitted as C 'lx_magic_buf = 0x00002020;'. Watcom 9.5a may re-emit this as an immediate store (MOV dword [slot],0x2020) instead of a rodata load; the two are runtime-equivalent. Behavior is identical for ALL inputs because the upper 2 slot bytes stay 0x0000 (never written by the 2-byte read), so the slot is always the NUL-terminated C string {magic0,magic1,0} and strcmp(&slot,"LX") (LX string @0x502f0 = 4c 58 00 00) compares only the first 3 bytes. The actual game LX magic 'LX' makes byte[2] irrelevant; any non-LX magic mismatches at byte0/byte1 regardless of the prefill. verify_method: post-build -d disasm to confirm the prefill value 0x2020 reaches the slot (immediate or rodata load) and the strcmp arg is &slot.
